title: Optical-Mass Water Gaussians for Per-Scene Underwater Rendering
abstract: Per-scene underwater reconstruction supports marine archaeology, seabed survey, and offshore inspection, but faces two coupled problems: attenuation and backscatter mix water effects with object appearance, and common 3D Gaussian Splatting renderers encode the medium globally, directionally, or on object surfaces, limiting spatial queries after camera motion. We propose AquaMass-GS (AM-GS), which couples an object-Gaussian scene model to normalized free-space water Gaussians. Cell-volume weighting gives direct-extinction and backscatter optical-mass semantics; analytic finite-path integration with coverage normalization queries water from camera to visible surface. Separate optimization and querying keep object appearance scene-tied while representing water by one equivalent coefficient per finite ray segment. On four SeaThru-NeRF development scenes, AM-GS provides competitive end-to-end novel-view quality, with the highest mean peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and the lowest learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS) among six methods; the observed margins over WaterSplatting (0.282 dB PSNR and 0.0002 LPIPS) are not statistically decisive under paired uncertainty, and its mean structural similarity (SSIM) is slightly lower. On paired simulation with hidden clean targets it improves medium-disabled SSIM by 0.1139 over WaterSplatting, and, in a controlled known-optics test using a compact sigma/Delta = 0.30 carrier, it reduces unseen-origin transmittance RMSE by 52.7% relative to a trilinear voxel carrier.
